label: dense positional ramp: late original-phase steps through <DEL>
explanation: Dense feature: active on about 43% of all steps and in nearly every sequence. Its main structure is positional. It never fires at t=0, is weak at t=1 (19%), and its rate climbs through the original phase to about 80% at orig_idx 5-6. It is most reliable at the <DEL> step (76% rate, 17% of mass). In the copy phase it falls to about 30%, with scattered moderate activations that the predicate misses (about 22% of mass). The largest activations are on the last few original tokens, the <DEL> step and the first one or two copy outputs, and top sequences often start with x. Token identity only weakly modulates it: inputs following g/o/r/j/k raise the rate to about 1.4x. Adding conditions on which tokens were seen, or on first occurrence, did not raise F1 above about 0.66. The predicate (original steps t>=2 plus <DEL>) gets dev F1 0.66 and mass recall 0.77, and many in-window steps are inactive.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (copy phase: h, x, m, 1; input phase: k, n, p, g; delimiter step: <DEL>) and the previous input (most: o, g, j, k, w, n; least: x, 1, m, -); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, t=4.
